tool.excerpt: Malaysia lifts emergency declaration in Sarawak's Serian Division as haze eases, but pollution persists elsewhere Investigative Opinion Politics Community Business ☰ Investigative Singapore International Opinion Politics Community Civil Society Business Malaysia Malaysia lifts emergency declaration in Sarawak's Serian Division as haze eases, but pollution persists elsewhere Malaysia has lifted the haze-related emergency in Sarawak’s Serian division after air quality improved, while cloud seeding and school closures continue amid smoke from fires in Kalimantan. Gutzy Asia 7 Sept 2026 AI-Generated Summary Malaysia lifted Serian’s emergency declaration after its air quality improved from hazardous to unhealthy levels. Samarahan recorded Malaysia’s only very unhealthy API reading on Monday morning, at 226. Sarawak extended cloud seeding while 647 schools temporarily shifted to home-based learning. Comments Share Malaysia has lifted the emergency declaration in Sarawak's Serian division after air quality improved from hazardous levels, while cloud-seeding operations have been extended as the state continues to deal with transboundary haze from fires in neighbouring Indonesia. Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim on Monday consented to lift the emergency declaration across Serian, which had been imposed on 4 September after air pollution in the division reached levels considered hazardous to public health and safety. The decision followed a decline in the Air Pollutant Index (API) in the area over the weekend. The move came as haze continued to affect several parts of Sarawak and other parts of Malaysia. As of 8am on Monday, Samarahan in Sarawak recorded the country's only “very unhealthy” API reading, at 226. A further 40 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy readings, while 24 were classified as moderate and two as good. Serian emergency lifted after air quality improves The emergency declaration covered the entire Serian division and was introduced after pollution levels rose sharply earlier in the week. Serian's API reached 518 at 10am on 4 September, placing the air quality in the hazardous category. Earlier readings that morning had already exceeded 500. The emergency was declared following advice from Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, Sarawak Premier Abang Johari Tun Openg and relevant government agencies.
